newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group rejects rival's attack claim.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group rejects rival's attack claim.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group denied on Friday it had attacked a rival militia, ending a nine-month-old ceasefire in northern Iraq between the two factions.

"There was no fighting between us and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and there was no ceasefire violation by us," Shazad Saib, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan's (PUK) Ankara representative told Reuters.
But a KDP statement faxed to Reuters on Friday said Jalal Talabani's PUK had kept up an offensive against KDP positions in the Roost valley on Thursday.
Massoud Barzani's KDP said on Wednesday Talabani's forces launched attacks on its bases on July 15-16 in Qasre region, near Iraq's border with Iran.
The two rival factions have held several rounds of peace talks in Ankara following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October.
Saib said the PUK was still committed to the ceasefire. "But if the KDP attacks us, we will defend ourselves." he said.
Many ceasefires between the two groups have been called and broken since the fighting first flared up in 1994.
The State Department said on Thursday the leaders of the two groups had told the United States they want to continue a ceasefire in the area despite the reported clashes.
The KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take control of the key Kurdish city of Arbil from Talabani's forces in fighting last August, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
The fighting gave Baghdad a foothold in northern Iraq for the first time since the end of the Gulf War in 1991 when the Kurds broke away and set up their own administration under Western air power.
